A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdamW-style Shampoo research. All 23 pages of v2 and 30 pages of v4 are readable, including v2's appendices and their retained, relocated material in v4.

before.justification: Figure 1 reports original stochastic quadratic simulations. Appendix E reports GPT-2 pretraining diagnostics on OpenWebText in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: Section 2.6 and Figure 1 report revised toy simulations. Section 5 retains the original GPT-2/OpenWebText results in Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 broadens its exponent constraint from 1/p + 1/q = 1 to 1/p + 1/q = 2−ω, with 0<ω≤2. This expands the allowable updates, including the momentum-SGD endpoint, while retaining the same momentum, preconditioner recursions, and weight-decay update.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same stochastic quadratic toy task and GPT-2 pretraining on OpenWebText. The revised toy constants are settings within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Both explicitly omit optimizer comparisons in their own experiments (v2 Appendix E.1; v4 Section 5.1). Comparisons involving AdamW, Muon, SOAP, and Splus remain attributed to prior work; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: For Figure 1, X1−X* changes from [[−1,−2],[2,1]] to [[−1,−3],[3,1]], the noise matrix A changes from all ones to all tens, and λ=10^-5 is added to the sweep. The objective, iteration budget, other optimizer settings, and GPT-2 training/logging protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing weight-decay sensitivity experiment is revised through changed initialization and noise, an additional λ value, and replacement curves. The gradient-norm-ratio and preconditioner spectral-floor analyses in Figures 2–3 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The stochastic-gradient-noise estimation procedure used for Figure 3 is also unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 1's curves change: v2 lists nonconvergence for λ=10^-1, 10^-2, and 10^-3; v4 additionally lists 10^-4 and reports a new 10^-5 trajectory. These results use revised settings, so they do not establish a same-setting performance change. Figures 2–3 and their findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: V4 adds Theorem 2 and its Section 4.5 proof, establishing an O(K^-ω/4) convergence bound for the powered singular-value measure under λ=0. It generalizes supporting inequalities and adds Lemma 8 proving finiteness of the required expectations. The original theorem is largely retained, while v2 Appendix A's steepest-descent variational derivations are removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion add a second central claim: convergence for preconditioning exponents beyond the original sum of 1/2, without decoupled weight decay. The original classical-exponent guarantee and its conditional comparison with optimal SGD convergence remain.

C2.justification: Section 3 explains why rates for different ω cannot be directly ordered. Remark 1 adds a spectral-norm-constrained optimization conjecture and explains the difficulty of extending weight decay across the generalized family. The broader non-Euclidean interpretation in v2 Appendix A is removed; existing practical-setting caveats remain.

D1.justification: The documented toy initialization, noise-matrix entries, and weight-decay sweep are revised. GPT-2 architecture, training recipe, logging procedure, eight-H200 hardware disclosure, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds references concerning Clarifying Shampoo, K-FAC, Muon with Newton-Schulz, and AdamW implicit bias, while removing the citation cluster accompanying Appendix A. The retained Gratton–Toint comparison now specifies its noise assumption and α-dependent rates. The main positioning against earlier Shampoo convergence analyses remains.

P1.justification: V4 substantially reorganizes the narrative: discussion paragraphs become numbered subsections, matrix lemmas and full proofs are integrated into Section 4, and Appendix E becomes Section 5 before the conclusion. The separate proof sketch, Appendix A, acknowledgements, and impact statement disappear, and the opening and conclusion are rewritten around two contributions.

P2.justification: The two-column main text and references become single-column, extensively changing equation and algorithm layout. Figure 1 is enlarged and redrawn with revised ticks and an additional legend entry. Figures 2–3 retain their graphical content but move from the appendix into the main document.

improvement.justification: Theorem 2 and its full proof substantially extend the paper's central theoretical applicability beyond the original exponent constraint, with unrestricted constant β for the zero-weight-decay case. Lemma 8 strengthens proof rigor by establishing required finite expectations, and the extension's limitations are explicit. These gains outweigh the loss of the peripheral steepest-descent discussion, while the original empirical support is retained.
